body.statement: Theorem 1. For every \(J\ge2\) and \(0\le s\le J\), averaging over \(G_J\) is lossless for the minimax problem. The full rectangular kernel has \(O(J^{20})\) rational entries of \(O(J)\) bit length and is exactly computable by coefficient recursion from \(F_h\). Moreover, \[R^*(J,s)=\min_{q,\eta}\max_{h\in\mathcal H_{J,s}}\sum_{n,o}q_nK_{hno}(\eta_{no}-\tau_h)^2=\max_{\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal H_{J,s})}\min_{n\in\mathcal N_J}B_n(\pi).\] An orbit law \(q\) belongs to \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s)\) if and only if there exist \(\eta\), \(\pi\), and \(v\) such that \(\mathcal R_h(q,\eta)\le v\) for every \(h\) and \(B_n(\pi)\ge v\) for every \(n\). This certificate decides membership of \(q^{\mathrm{pair}}\), \(q^{\mathrm{Ber}}\), and \(\mathcal C_J\), essential noncanonicality, and singleton uniqueness by coordinate optimization over the projected optimal face.
body.justification: The full primal--dual contact system, rather than the value alone, is needed to distinguish canonical and correlated minimax designs.

body.consumer: For each analyst-selected sensitivity value \(s\), a trial designer can enumerate the exact minimax assignment laws and select one satisfying operational support or balance constraints without losing minimaxity for \(\Theta_{J,s}\).
